title: Valid Tree Graph
statement:
Decide whether an undirected graph is a single tree.

Contract
- Nodes are numbered `0` through `nodeCount - 1`, where `nodeCount >= 1`. Each entry of `edges` is a pair `{a, b}` of valid nodes describing an undirected edge.
- Return true exactly when the graph is connected and contains no cycle.
- A repeated edge or a self-loop counts as a cycle.
- Do not modify `edges`.

Examples
- `isTree(1, new int[0][2])` returns true.
- `isTree(3, new int[][]{{0, 1}, {1, 2}})` returns true.
- `isTree(3, new int[][]{{0, 1}, {1, 2}, {2, 0}})` returns false.
hints: A tree on n nodes has a very specific number of edges. Checking that count rules out many inputs immediately.
The right edge count is not enough: a cycle can coexist with a disconnected node. Make sure no edge joins two nodes that are already connected.

Process edges with union-find and fail when an edge joins nodes already in the same set (or search from node 0 and check every node is reached). Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space, where n is the number of nodes (edges beyond n - 1 are rejected immediately).
inputSyntax: Input: node count, then undirected edges as a-b between nodes 0..count-1, for example: 5 0-1 0-2 0-3 1-4
